resources.string: I understand Life Load is a general wellness and self-tracking tool. It does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, or emergency support, and it is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, prevent, or mitigate disease. I will consult a qualified healthcare professional for medical concerns.

Life Load is not trying to label a day as good or bad. It helps you notice when sleep, stress, pain, food, work, family load, and evening habits start combining into a pattern that may need a smaller next step.

The formula keeps guidance consistent. It turns repeated signals into a simple state such as Stable, Watch, or Recovery priority. It also lowers guidance quality when important details are missing, so the app does not sound more certain than the data supports.

One late night may not matter much. Late phone use plus project overrun plus high stress can point toward a lighter evening. Strong recovery can offset some load, but repeated risk signals can still push the pattern upward. Missing pain, stress, or energy makes guidance less reliable.

The app uses ideas from behavior-change research: self-monitoring, feedback, small concrete next steps, and if-then planning. These methods work best when they help you choose a specific action rather than just showing numbers.

Life Load is not a diagnosis, treatment plan, or emergency tool. It is a personal pattern and recovery-planning aid. If something feels medically urgent or unsafe, use appropriate medical or emergency support.

This is a conservative decision-support score for consistency, recovery, and anti-overreach. It is not a medical diagnosis.
Training context: ATL 7d %1$s · CTL 42d %2$s · ratio %3$s · ramp %4$s
Life load = strain + training load. Recovery is shown separately so a hard day can still be acceptable if recovery is strong enough.

Manual activity, saved activity rows, and Garmin activities feed the same duration-sensitive rollup. Bike commute is lighter than sport biking; runs and CrossFit count more than both. Matching manual/Garmin activity rows are deduplicated.
ATL is a 7-day activity load and CTL is a 42-day activity base. Big training from a low base, or acute load far above chronic load, adds strain support signals.

Stress, pain, missed sleep, missed after-work decompression, evening sequence support, relationship stress, being alone at home, late phone, project overrun, heavy work, family stress, alcohol exposure, eating episodes, migraine signals, Garmin high stress, and short sleep add strain.
Sleep on time, clean nutrition, energy, mood, shutdown, decompression, an after-work reset, rehab, walks, and reasonable steps add recovery. Garmin sleep helps when manual sleep is unknown.
Alcohol at home, eating episodes, migraine signals, and pain flares override optimism. The response should prioritize recovery, not punishment training.

Planning research: a 26-study physical-activity meta-analysis found a small-to-medium effect for if-then plans (g=0.31; 95%% CI 0.11-0.51). Source: Bélanger-Gravel et al., 2013.
Planning research: follow-up effects for if-then plans remained positive in the same review (g=0.24; 95%% CI 0.13-0.35). Source: Bélanger-Gravel et al., 2013.
mHealth research: one app experiment found self-affirmation boosters improved goal adherence (P=.04). Source: Springer et al., 2018.
mHealth review: common behavior-change tools included self-monitoring, performance feedback, and tailored messages. Source: Schoeppe et al., 2016.
